summary: @servicetitan/microfront preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases (bun-v1.3.13), extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB heavily obfuscated blob using a rotated string-array constant table and a decoder function (obfuscator.io-style: `var MmgoCP,...;function WV8StW(...){...MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift());return MmgoCP}` followed by a large mixed constant array and a decoder), with no source map, imports, or readable strings. Fetching a second JS runtime at install to execute an opaque sibling payload runs attacker-controlled code on the installer at `npm install` time and bypasses Node-based inspection of the executed logic. The package advertises itself as a React MicroFrontEnd library, which does not require an alternate JS runtime. The repository URL `github.com/servicetitan/playground.git` does not correspond to a real ServiceTitan repository, and the `@servicetitan/*` scope usage appears to impersonate the ServiceTitan organization.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
